clue.text: International underground in place of experiment

parts.note: an international match in cricket or rugby is a Test
the Tube is London's underground railway

explanation.surface: Some international underground organisation stands in for an experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory glass tube is the vessel in which a chemical experiment is carried out.

clue.text: Farewell to uncanned music!

indicators.note: read as un-CAN-ned, the letters spelling the word can are taken out of the music

parts.note: a cantata is a choral piece of music

explanation.surface: A goodbye to recorded music in favour of the live kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncanned' looks like 'live, not recorded', but it means remove CAN: CANTATA without CAN leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is a casual British way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Set off such as 14 on the top spot

parts.note: to set off on a journey is to start
14-down is a Grecian urn, so it is an example of an urn

explanation.surface: A famous vase is given pride of place on a stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The '14' points to 14-down, the Grecian urn of Keats's ode.
explanation.definitionFit: A star turn is the headline act, the top spot on a variety bill.

clue.text: Acknowledgement setter almost demands from island

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
the setter refers to themselves as I

indicators.note: the last part of the word for demands is cut off, an Araucarian liberty of two letters

parts.note: demands as a verb means wants

explanation.surface: Thanks, the setter nearly demands of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' here removes two letters, TS, from WANTS, leaving WAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiwan is a large island off the south-east coast of China.

clue.text: What 14 says to make us eat it by having compassion and vice versa: 9 we 8

indicators.note: the letters are reworked to make something new

parts.note: ruth is an old word for pity or compassion

explanation.surface: A gnomic recipe telling us to eat something with compassion, with a coded line of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats's urn says 'Beauty is truth, truth beauty': 'and vice versa' gives the second half, and '9 we 8' gives 'that is all ye need to know' (9-across, 8-down), completing the quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the words Keats has the Grecian urn speak at the close of his ode.

clue.text: Stir its top into a bit of brain

indicators.note: one piece is put into the other

parts.note: a prion is an infectious protein found in the brain

indicators.note: its refers back to the first word, whose top letter is taken

explanation.surface: Stir the top of it into a piece of brain, like a cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Its top' is the first letter of Stir, S, put into PRION. The blog thought 'bit of brain' loose for a prion.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is British slang for jail.

clue.text: Followed in post with a weight off one's mind

definitions.meaning: to relieve a sentry or official is to take over their post

definitions.text: with a weight off one's mind

explanation.definitionFit: Relieved means both taken over from at a post and freed from anxiety.

clue.text: Disparagement of the unattainable like this impels accepting knock

parts.note: so means in this way

indicators.note: one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: impels means urges
a rap is a knock

explanation.surface: Such disparagement drives one to take a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: From Aesop's fox, who called the grapes he could not reach sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sour grapes is the idiom for belittling what one cannot have.

clue.text: Basis for disclosure from organiser of "No don't" Week

indicators.note: the letters are organised into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone organises a week of refusals.
explanation.definitionFit: On a need-to-know basis, secret information is disclosed only to those who require it.

clue.text: See Bangkok people about their leader's completely final statement

indicators.note: the people go round the other piece

parts.note: Bangkok is the capital of Thailand, whose people are Thais

indicators.note: a leader is a first letter

parts.note: all means completely

explanation.surface: Look how the people of Bangkok gather round their leader.
explanation.definitionFit: That is all is the phrase that ends a statement or briefing.

clue.text: Coleridge's 5 was inferior, about 1m to be raised

indicators.note: the comparative goes round the other pieces

parts.note: lower means ranked below, as in was lower
1 is I and m is metre, so one metre

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Coleridge's prison was a lowly place, a metre in height.
explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge's poem is 'This Lime-Tree Bower My Prison' (5-across). 'Raised' turns BE upwards in this down entry, and 'about' wraps the comparative round the metre and that.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge called the lime-tree bower his prison in the title of his poem.

clue.text: Parasite left on river

parts.note: the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A parasite sits on the left bank of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A louse is a small wingless insect that lives on its host.

clue.text: Don't allow Scots boy and old man to keep English boxer

parts.note: to ban is not to allow
Tam is the Scots form of Tom

indicators.note: the old man holds the English piece within

parts.note: wight is an archaic word for a person

explanation.surface: A ban on a Scottish lad and his father keeping an English fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantamweight boxer fights in a light weight division.

clue.text: Revolutionary on ship — on ship where men are moved

parts.note: Che Guevara, the revolutionary
SS is a steamship
to board is to ship, to go aboard

explanation.surface: A revolutionary aboard ship, then on a ship again.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second 'ship' and BOARD as verbs meaning embark.
explanation.definitionFit: Chessmen are moved around the squares of the board.

clue.text: Recovered by awfully uncaring bride of Keats

indicators.note: read Recovered as Re covered, the first piece inside
awfully signals the letters in bad order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bride recovered after an awfully uncaring husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats addresses the urn as 'Thou still unravish'd bride of quietness'.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats's ode opens by calling the urn a bride.

clue.text: Leading man's lady love

parts.note: her stands for a lady
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: The leading man's sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at Hero, the lady love of Leander.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero is the principal male character in a story or play.

clue.text: Retire — after success comes dismissal

parts.note: a hit is a success
the sack is dismissal from a job

explanation.surface: Retiring after a success brings dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hit the sack is slang for going to bed.

clue.text: The EU's vegetable?

definitions.meaning: the European Union's main seat is in the Belgian capital

explanation.definitionFit: Brussels is the EU's headquarters city and the name of a sprout.

clue.text: Direction to towns, including old one, with assets

parts.note: SE is south-east

indicators.note: the towns take the old one inside

parts.note: cities are large towns
Ur was an ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: Instructions to the towns, including an old one, about their assets.
explanation.definitionFit: Securities are stocks, bonds and other financial assets.

clue.text: Fiend's unfinished protest

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its ending, so the final letter of the fiend is dropped

parts.note: a fiend is a demon

explanation.surface: A demon's protest left incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is short for a demonstration, a protest march.

clue.text: Painter of amazing resourcefulness

indicators.note: the painter is made of letters from the words

explanation.surface: An artist of extraordinary ingenuity.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingres was a French Neoclassical painter.

clue.text: Money for massage makes impression in church

parts.note: brass is British slang for money
a rubbing is a massage

explanation.surface: Paying for a massage makes a good impression at church.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass rubbing is a copy made by rubbing over a memorial brass in a church.

clue.text: Girl with lisp? I don't believe it!

indicators.note: a lisp turns the s sounds into th

parts.note: a girl is a miss

explanation.surface: A lisping girl's exclamation of disbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: Myth is used to dismiss a claim as untrue.

clue.text: See 2
Since solver's heard it's blue

indicators.note: heard signals the words are spoken

parts.note: since you are, as you're

explanation.surface: Since the solver is blue, they hear it.
explanation.definitionFit: Azure is a bright sky blue.

clue.text: Manufactured hooey about fighting turn to question of health

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the fighting
manufactured means made up, so rearranged

parts.note: fighting is war
U as in U-turn

explanation.surface: Made-up nonsense about fighting leads to a health query.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manufactured' makes HOEYO, which 'about' wraps round the fighting, with the U-turn last.
explanation.definitionFit: How are you? is a question about someone's health.

clue.text: Bacon may be article in container

indicators.note: the article goes inside the container

parts.note: a dish is a container
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Bacon can be an item in a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish bacon is a familiar type from Denmark.

clue.text: Large French female accepting 100 little old coins

indicators.note: the words take in the hundred

parts.note: gros is French for large
a hen is a female bird
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A large French woman accepting a hundred old coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Groschen were small old German and Austrian coins.
